correctness.rationale: The KKT matrix is invertible with determinant c² and zero satisfies the saddle inequalities. Inverting I+τS gives D=(I−K)/ρ=[(s²+h,−s);(s(1−h),s²)]/(1+s²). Its trace is t and its determinant is s²/(1+s²)=d. Real roots μ± are positive, so the exact Schur limit is ρ<2/μ+, and the maximum modulus is minimized uniquely by balancing the opposed endpoints at ρ=2/t. For conjugate roots the squared radius is 1−ρt+ρ²d, giving the strict interval and the unique minimizer t/(2d). At the repeated root the strict limit is 4/t and the radius is zero only at 2/t; at each extreme stability boundary at least one eigenvalue has modulus one. A fixed K terminates universally in finite time iff both eigenvalues vanish, requiring Δ=0; factoring the discriminant numerator gives τ²[q²+4c²(τq−1)], with exactly one positive root iff q<2c. At that root the positive (1,2) entry prevents index one, and Cayley–Hamilton gives index two. Exact alternate replay: with ζ=q/(2c) at the terminating tuning, K=(2ζ/(1+ζ²))(1,ζ)ᵀ(−ζ,1), whose square vanishes since the row and column pair to zero. At ζ=3/4 this produces all four rational entries in the finding exactly. Solving ρ*>2 gives ζ>1/√3. These checks apply to all deterministic starts, not only eigenvector starts or monotonic norm decay. Supplied code and run description were inspected and not executed.
residual_risks: Exact arithmetic and fixed positive parameters are essential for the termination claim. No finite-precision accuracy or multi-mode extension is established.

value.rationale: The spectral formulas alone are standard two-eigenvalue analysis. The smallest curved bilinear saddle model gives an exact separation between generic sufficient relaxation rules and what a fixed natural splitting can achieve: there is a precise curvature threshold for hitting the saddle from every start in two steps, and it can occur for relaxation greater than two. At the nilpotent tuning the displayed rank-one factorization gives ‖K‖₂=2ζ=q/c, which can exceed one despite exact termination. This is a precise witness distinguishing spectral behavior from per-step contraction, not a claim that extrapolation is generally numerically safe.
residual_risks: The useful boundary is for the stated planar iteration; no implication for anchored ADMM or broad finite-precision practice is claimed.
